final_recommendation: The room converged on a narrow trilateral deal by late September 2018 (65% probability) with Canada accepting the U.S.-Mexico auto terms, granting 3-4% dairy market access, preserving Chapter 19 in modified form, and converting the sunset clause to a periodic review mechanism. The two decisive blocking risks are Canadian dairy concessions and Chapter 19 dispute settlement, with labor enforcement credibility emerging as the critical downstream U.S. ratification constraint.
minority_objections: 25% probability talks stall through October if Canada refuses adequate dairy concessions or Chapter 19 impasse occurs
Hardline anti-Chapter 19 Republicans will oppose preservation as USTR failure
AFL-CIO may oppose if labor enforcement mechanisms deemed weak or unverifiable
key_conflicts: U.S. demand for substantial Canadian dairy access vs. Canada's supply management political untouchability (Tier 1 deal-breaker)
USTR objective to eliminate Chapter 19 vs. Canadian red line to preserve it (direct collision, Tier 1 deal-breaker)
U.S. demand for automatic sunset vs. auto industry need for investment certainty
Democratic House demand for enforceable Mexico labor standards vs. Mexico sovereignty concerns
U.S. dairy lobby demand for 3.5-4% access vs. Canadian rural Liberal MP constituent pressure
key_concessions: USTR accepts Chapter 19 survival in exchange for dairy access, Mexico labor enforcement, and Canada accepting U.S.-Mexico auto terms
Sunset clause converted to periodic review mechanism (16-year term, 6-year reviews) without automatic termination
Canada grants 3-4% dairy market access framed as TPP-equivalent plus
Canada accepts U.S.-Mexico auto terms (~75% RVC + labor-value content) without reopening
Mexico already conceded higher RVC, labor-value content, and enforceable labor standards in bilateral
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 elimination is likely walk-away, politically too costly domestically
Canada: Total dairy capitulation is government-threatening
U.S. Congress/Labor: Will oppose deal if labor enforcement is weak/unverifiable
Auto industry: Hard 5-year sunset creates investment paralysis and industry opposition that kills deal
USTR: Must show material improvement over NAFTA 1.0, cannot appear weak on Canada
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Timing risk of Canadian election being called before ratification, turning deal into political football
Delay of U.S. ratification into 2020 presidential election cycle contaminating the vote
Spillover effects of auto-RVC rule changes on broader supply chains (electronics, aerospace, machinery)
Risk that even modest dairy concession triggers Canadian political backlash imperiling ratification despite compensation package
downstream_risk_variables: Mexico passes constitutional labor reform before U.S. ratification vote (timing uncertain with López Obrador transition)
Democratic House majority post-November 2018 midterms changes ratification dynamics
AFL-CIO position on final labor enforcement mechanism determines Democratic caucus votes
U.S. dairy lobby assessment of whether 3-4% Canadian access is sufficient
Canadian rural Liberal MP reaction to dairy concessions and constituent pressure
Whether USTR can frame Chapter 19 survival as acceptable trade-off domestically
uncertainty_notes: The meeting identified dairy and Chapter 19 as the two decisive blocking points but expressed 65% confidence in resolution. Critical uncertainties include: whether 3-4% dairy access satisfies both U.S. agriculture lobby and survives Canadian domestic politics; whether labor enforcement mechanism specifics (facility-level vs. systemic-only) will satisfy AFL-CIO and Democratic House; timing of Mexico labor reform implementation; and whether post-midterm Democratic House majority fundamentally changes U.S. ratification calculus. The review-mechanism compromise on sunset appears highly likely to bridge that gap.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: Discussed as Tier 2 secondary bottleneck (manageable via technical side letters and phase-in), not a deal-breaker; core terms already locked in U.S.-Mexico bilateral
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Identified as HIGHEST RISK for U.S. ratification; specific enforcement mechanism design (facility-level vs. systemic) drives Democratic House support; AFL-CIO opposition scenario explicitly causes deal failure
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Rated Tier 1 DECISIVE bottleneck, five-star priority, explicitly called 'single most likely collapse point'; drives Canada's concession of 3-4% access in base-case package
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Rated Tier 1 DECISIVE bottleneck with direct collision; Canadian red line drives USTR concession to preserve Chapter 19 in exchange for dairy and other wins
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset identified as creating investment paralysis and industry opposition that kills deal; drives specific compromise of 16-year term with 6-year reviews; 'highly likely' resolution
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Entire Tier 3 section dedicated to downstream ratification risks; labor enforcement credibility, dairy sufficiency, and Chapter 19 opposition explicitly shape what must be in the deal text now
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto industry concerns about compliance cost, phase-in periods, and grandfathering raised; broader manufacturers concerned about cascading origin disputes; but limited leverage and secondary to core issues
